SaaStr let AI send the volume while people handled the replies. Here is what they actually reported and what they did not.

SaaStr said a top human SDR sent 285 emails a month. Their AI sent 3221 emails a month with a similar response rate. Same kind of message and same kind of list but far more of it. These are SaaStrs own numbers so treat them as a case study and not a promise.

The lesson is simple. AI multiplies a playbook that already works. If your list or your offer is weak then ten times more sending only gives you ten times more silence.

The guide shows the 4 step setup where AI writes and sends and you handle every reply. It also covers the guardrails that keep you out of spam and a prompt that writes in your voice.

Vercel had 10 people working inbound leads. Now one person checks the work of an AI agent and the other nine moved to outbound.

Their COO shared the story on Lennys Podcast. The agent reads a new lead and researches the person and the company and decides if they look qualified and drafts a reply. A human still checks it before it goes out.

Why it worked. Inbound lead work is the same steps every time. It is easy to write down so it is easy for AI to copy. The hard part is starting new conversations with strangers and people still do that.

Speed matters too. A form that sits in a queue overnight goes cold.

The guide gives you a 6 step plan to build your own lead triage agent with no code tools plus the fit rules and a copy paste prompt that scores a lead.

Email the companies that look like your rivals customers.

An agency called The Kiln used this play to help one client build four to five million dollars in new pipeline according to a Smartlead case study.

Why it works. These companies already buy this kind of product so you do not have to explain the problem. And you have an easy reason to write. Most senders ignore them.

The 5 steps in the guide:
1. Pick 3 rivals your buyers compare you with
2. Collect their public customers and build a lookalike list
3. Email the companies with fresh signals first
4. Add one real detail about each person
5. Warm up slowly and never trash the competitor

Talk about the result you give and not about what is wrong with them.

Cold email versus the spam filter. Most emails lose before anyone reads them and the cause is usually settings and not copy.

Gmail and Outlook decide in a split second if your email is real mail or spam. Win with these 3 settings.

Round 1. Use your own sending domain with SPF and DKIM and DMARC set up. Do not send cold email from your main domain.

Round 2. Turn open tracking off. That tiny hidden image makes filters suspicious. Turn link tracking off too.

Round 3. Plain text and no links and about 30 a day per inbox. Real people do not send 500 emails a day from one inbox.

The guide has the exact steps for each round and how to check your spam rate for free.

Someone replied I am not the right person. Most people move on. That reply is good news.

That person just told you the company is real and the email works and someone else owns the problem. They know who it is. You only have to ask.

The 4 steps in the guide:
1. Ask one short question. Who is the right person for this
2. Email the new person and say who sent you
3. Put the same question in your follow up
4. Tag these leads so none get lost

Do not re pitch and do not ask for a meeting in step one. One question only. The guide has the exact emails to copy.
